common_name: Snippet Dark Pink Weigela (Dwarf Reblooming Pink-Flowered Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown Snippet Dark Pink in spring to early summer in well-drained soil in full sun; this dwarf Weigela series was bred to flower continuously without deadheading, so give it a true six-plus hours of direct sun for the heaviest rebloom.

directions: Snippet Dark Pink packs the reblooming habit of larger Weigela introductions into a knee-high, rounded plant suited to foundation beds and containers. Dark pink, trumpet-shaped flowers open in a heavy late-spring flush and continue sporadically into summer on new growth, without the need for deadheading to keep the cycle going. Give it a full-sun site with good drainage, since dense dark-green foliage and the tightest flowering habit depend on strong light exposure. Prune lightly right after the first big bloom flush if reshaping is needed, rather than shearing hard, to avoid cutting off developing summer buds.

common_name: Summer Wine Black Ninebark (Compact Near-Black Foliage Ninebark)

planting.note: Plant in average to moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Summer Wine Black holds its darkest near-black leaf color only with strong direct light and benefits from open spacing for air circulation.

directions: Summer Wine Black pushes the dark-leaf ninebark trend further than earlier Summer Wine and Diabolo selections, holding a deeper, almost true-black leaf color through the growing season rather than fading to purple-green. Clusters of small white spring flowers stand out sharply against the near-black foliage before giving way to reddish seed capsules. Like other ninebark cultivars it tolerates clay, periodic wet feet, and urban soils, but needs generous spacing and good airflow to avoid foliar disease in humid climates. Renewal-prune by removing the oldest third of stems at the base every couple of years rather than shearing the whole plant.

common_name: Lil Ditty Witherod Viburnum (Dwarf Native Viburnum with Fragrant White Flowers)

planting.note: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in partial sun to sun; this dwarf witherod viburnum fits small beds and foundation plantings where the full-size native species would outgrow the space.

directions: Lil Ditty shrinks the native witherod viburnum down to a knee-high, rounded shrub without losing the species' fragrant, creamy-white flower clusters, which open in late spring and are followed by berries that shift from pink to blue-black when cross-pollinated. Its small scale and tolerance of part shade make it a good fit for shrub borders and foundation beds under high canopy where larger viburnums would crowd neighboring plants. It is notably deer-resistant compared with many flowering shrubs and prefers consistently moist, humus-rich soil. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since next year's buds set soon after the current bloom finishes.

common_name: Scentara Double Blue Lilac (Fragrant Double-Flowered Early Lilac)

planting.note: Plant in full sun in well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil; Scentara Double Blue needs a real winter chill and open airflow to bloom well and resist powdery mildew, like other hyacinthiflora lilacs.

directions: Scentara Double Blue was named a Proven Winners Flowering Shrub of the Year for its unusually full, double purplish-blue flower clusters, a step up in petal count from typical single-flowered lilacs, carrying the same strong classic lilac fragrance. It flowers once in mid to late spring on a large, upright, cold-hardy shrub rated down to zone 2, making it an option for lilac fans in climates too harsh for many hybrid lilacs. Give it full sun, good drainage, and soil on the neutral-to-alkaline side, since lilacs sulk in acidic, poorly drained ground. Prune immediately after flowering, since next year's buds form on the current season's new wood soon after bloom ends.

common_name: Dandy Man Purple Rhododendron (Northern-Hardy Large-Flowered Purple Rhododendron)

planting.note: Plant in acidic, moist, well-drained soil (pH 5.5-7.5) in partial sun to sun; Dandy Man Purple was bred and field-tested for reliable bud hardiness in cold northern climates, including Maine and New Hampshire trial sites.

directions: Dandy Man Purple is a large-flowered hybrid rhododendron bred specifically for improved cold-hardiness of its flower buds, so it keeps blooming reliably in regions where late-winter freezes often blast the buds on older rhododendron cultivars. It carries rich purple trusses across the early, mid, and late spring rhododendron bloom window, giving an extended show when planted alongside other timing selections. Evergreen foliage provides year-round structure in a woodland or shaded foundation planting, but it needs consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil and resents heavy clay or alkaline ground. Mulch to keep roots cool and moist, and avoid shearing, since old flower trusses should be snapped off by hand rather than cut to protect next year's buds just below them.

common_name: Pucker Up Red Twig Dogwood (Quilted-Leaf Red-Stemmed Dogwood)

planting.note: Plant in moist to wet, well-drained soil in partial sun to sun; Pucker Up tolerates damp low spots and streambanks better than most ornamental shrubs, fitting rain gardens and pond edges.

directions: Pucker Up stands out among red twig dogwoods for its heavily textured, quilted-looking green leaves, a foliage effect that carries the shrub's interest through the growing season before the bright red young stems take over for winter display. Small white flower clusters open in spring, but the main appeal is structural: dense, bushy, compact growth to only about three to four feet, more manageable than taller red twig dogwood cultivars. It tolerates wet, poorly drained soil better than most shrubs, making it useful on stream edges and in low, soggy parts of the landscape. Cut out a portion of the oldest stems each late winter, since the brightest red winter color comes from young, first- and second-year wood.
